Correct the visible rightward handle offset while tracking the belt. Add slight surface clearance, then close across the middle of the handle rather than near the frog head.

Correct the remaining small rightward offset, descend 12 mm to enclose the middle handle, and close while tracking the belt. Make a small vertical test lift with gripper held closed.
The handle now remains visibly enclosed by both jaws during the short lift. Keep the right gripper closed and raise vertically another 12 cm, verifying retention from RGB.
The rattle slipped and shifted toward the near edge of the belt. Reopen and reapproach its new lane, descending while tracking rightward; retention was not achieved.
Move toward the handle rather than the broad frog head, correcting lateral offset and approaching slowly after contact-related tracking error. Close while following the belt.
Let the fully closed command settle around the visible handle, then test retention with a slow 3.6 cm lift while tapering conveyor tracking.
No retained lift is visible. Reopen and recenter farther right and forward around the wider frog head/neck, approaching slowly before closing.

The frog head remains visibly seated between both jaws during the test lift. Keep the gripper commanded closed and raise another 10 cm with a small inward motion for reach margin.
The lift stopped at an IK limit after four steps. Replan from the observed pose: keep the frog head clamped and retract inward with only a small rise to regain joint margin.
The inward command was rejected before any motion. Retry with much smaller horizontal increments and no rise, keeping the held object closed and configuration continuous.
Small retraction restored joint margin. The frog remains between the jaws; maintain closure and lift gradually while retracting inward to avoid the reach limit.
The frog slipped back onto the belt and rotated. Reopen and descend toward its visible head for a deeper enclosing grasp, preserving the elbow-up configuration.
The target is now at the near edge below the wrist view. Shift the open gripper toward the robot and follow rightward to recover visual alignment, without further descent.
The rotated frog head is visible at the near edge. Move rearward to enclose its broader body, descend slightly, and close while following the belt; preserve configuration continuity.
The frog head is between the jaws. Maintain full closure, briefly settle, then lift slowly with inward retraction for joint margin; verify retention in the wrist view.
The head slipped outside the closed jaws. Reopen and enclose it more deeply with a small rightward correction, then close without lifting yet; monitor reach and contact.

Replan after the continuity rejection: retract slightly and move rearward, gently tilting the gripper toward the visible head instead of extending the arm farther. Close only after this small approach.
The prior attempt executed zero steps. Reduce both translation and tilt increments substantially to recover configuration continuity with the gripper open.

The rotated frog head is centered between both jaws. Maintain full closure, settle briefly, then make a slow inward-and-upward test lift while preserving reach margin.
The frog head remains seated between the jaws as the background drops, indicating retention during the test lift. Keep closure and lift another 9 cm with inward retraction for reach margin.
